cases.name: Fisher v. University of Texas (2013)

components.decision: Vacated and remanded for application of proper strict scrutiny.
components.scope: The Court resolved the review standard without finally deciding whether this admissions plan was lawful.
components.locator: Kennedy majority opinion Part III and closing paragraph.
components.survey_fit: General affirmative-action preferences do not decide how a court should apply strict scrutiny.

cases.interpretation_limit: This is not a final yes/no ruling on the program. The procedural label here refers to that policy comparison, not an absence of legal substance.

cases.name: Fisher v. University of Texas (2016)

components.decision: Upheld the challenged race-conscious admissions plan under equal protection.
components.scope: Race as one factor in holistic review alongside a percentage-admission pathway; the Court upheld this particular program and record, not every racial preference.
components.survey_fit: Pew asks about increasing campus representation; Gallup asks about considering race against a merit-only alternative. Both concern higher education, but neither describes Texas’s percentage pathway, holistic review, or constitutional test. Keep the two questions separate and contextual.

cases.interpretation_limit: Different wording, years and survey designs prevent interpreting the percentages as a trend or an isolated wording effect. The 2013 Gallup and 2014 Pew fieldwork preceded Fisher II; Gallup’s June–July 2016 survey straddled the decision and is not used.

cases.name: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard / UNC

components.decision: Invalidated the challenged race-conscious admissions programs.
components.scope: Limits those uses of race; does not prohibit considering an individual’s account of how race affected their life. Military academies were not decided.
components.locator: Roberts majority opinion Parts III–VI; footnote 4.
components.survey_fit: VOTER combines women and racial minorities and does not specify admissions. Its 2020 responses do not directly measure approval of the 2023 holdings.

components.decision: Invalidated the challenged race-conscious admissions programs.
components.scope: Limits those uses of race; does not prohibit considering an individual’s account of how race affected their life. Military academies were not decided.
components.locator: Roberts majority opinion Parts III–VI; footnote 4.
components.survey_fit: The question isolates race and ethnicity in selective-college admissions for diversity. It does not describe Harvard’s or UNC’s particular programs, so this remains context rather than a case-approval estimate.

cases.interpretation_limit: The two companion cases are one displayed event, not two independent survey comparisons. Broad affirmative-action opinion cannot establish exact-case agreement.
